summary: The highest measured killing rate in the country (24.7 per 100k trans women/yr reported; 11.6 per 100k recorded — a floor, not a total) and a damning institutional response: after a mob of ~10 beat a trans couple outside a women's restroom in Benton (31 May 2026), no alleged attacker was arrested and both victims were criminally charged (disturbing the peace; one jailed in a men's facility, searched by a male guard despite a female marker on her licence). The Bossier Parish governing body then unanimously approved — on the first of two required votes, 15 July 2026, reportedly at the sheriff's request — a local ordinance to criminalise trans restroom use, one of the most punitive in the country: Louisiana has no statewide adult bathroom ban, so this local law is the sharpest instrument in the state. A trans inmate was killed at Angola state prison (2 April 2024); killings continue into 2026. Well below the national score 0.36.

sources.summary: Investigative data story overlaying state legal-risk maps on the TGEU Trans Murder Monitoring record (2008-2025, 428 US victims): per-100k trans women/yr killing rates by state. Louisiana holds the highest reported rate (24.7; 11.6 recorded) despite the undercount, but a 'safest-state' (Maryland, 23.5) ranks second and a 'do not travel' framing does not sort by law — legislative risk predicts state behaviour, not physical safety.

Reports the 31 May 2026 mob beating of trans couple Aurora Rush and Shae Sanders at Cypress Black Bayou Park, Benton, Louisiana: ~10 attackers, no arrests among them, while Rush was charged with two counts of disturbing the peace (up to a year each) and Sanders one count, after Rush was jailed in a men's facility and searched by a male guard despite a female licence marker. On 15 July 2026 the Bossier Parish Police Jury unanimously approved a proposed anti-trans restroom ordinance on the first of two votes, reportedly requested by the parish sheriff; victims' counsel frames the attack as a hate crime.

Investigative account (5 Aug 2026) of the same park attack: notes Louisiana has no statewide anti-trans bathroom ban, so the couple's restroom use was legal; confirms both victims charged and one taken to a men's jail, no attackers arrested, and that the parish municipality 'voted for one of the most severe anti-trans bathroom ordinances in the country' at the sheriff's instance.

Human Rights Campaign memorial (11 June 2024) for Yella (Robert) Clark Jr., a 45-year-old Black transgender person serving a life sentence, killed by other inmates at Angola prison on 2 April 2024 — HRC's at-least-16th violent killing of a trans or gender-expansive person that year; documents earlier targeted-risk history in custody and persistent misgendering in initial reporting.

tangentialFactors: Statewide K-12/facility ban (2024) and a state binary-'sex' definition law (2026) set the legal frame that emboldened the parish ordinance and the 'protecting the children' framing of the mob (dossier; MAP equality map).
